AND quest_id = ?\",\n        (camp_id, quest_id),\n    ).fetchone()[\"cnt\"]\n    done = conn.execute(\n        \"SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM quest_milestones \"\n        \"WHERE campaign_id = ? AND quest_id = ? AND done = 1\",\n        (camp_id, quest_id),\n    ).fetchone()[\"cnt\"]\n    return total, done\n\n\ndef _get_quest(camp_id, quest_id):\n    \"\"\"Return a quest with milestone counts, or None if missing.\"\"\"\n    with _get_db() as conn:\n        row = conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT quest_id, title, status FROM quests WHERE campaign_id = ? AND quest_id = ?\",\n            (camp_id, quest_id),\n        ).fetchone() is not None:\n            return False\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO quests (campaign_id, quest_id, title, status) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (camp_id, quest_id, title, status),\n        )\n        for milestone in unique_milestones:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO quest_milestones (campaign_id, quest_id, milestone, done) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                (camp_id, quest_id, milestone, 0),\n            )\n        conn.commit()\n    return _get_quest(camp_id, quest_id)\n\n\ndef update_quest_progress(camp_id, quest_id, completed):\n    \"\"\"Mark the listed milestones as done for a quest.\n\n    Returns the quest progress summary on success, None if the quest is\n    missing, or False if the milestone list is invalid.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(completed, list):\n        return False\n\n    with _get_db() as conn:\n        if conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT 1 FROM quests WHERE campaign_id = ? AND project_id = ?\",\n            (camp_id, project_id),\n        ).fetchone()\n        if row is None:\n            return None\n        if row[\"status\"] != \"active\":\n            return False\n\n        new_completed = min(row[\"days_completed\"] + days, row[\"days_required\"])\n        status = \"complete\" if new_completed >= row[\"days_required\"] else \"active\"\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE crafting_projects SET days_completed = ?, status = ? \"\n            \"WHERE campaign_id = ? AND project_id = ?\",\n            (new_completed, status, camp_id, project_id),\n        )\n\n        if status == \"complete\":\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO campaign_inventory (campaign_id, item_slug, quantity, owner, source) \"\n                \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'crafting') \"\n                \"ON CONFLICT(campaign_id, item_slug, owner) \"\n                \"DO UPDATE SET quantity = quantity + excluded.quantity\",\n                (camp_id, row[\"item_slug\"], 1, row[\"character_id\"]),\n            )\n        conn.commit()\n\n    return {\"id\": project_id, \"days_completed\": new_completed, \"status\": status}\n\n\n# --- Session scheduling ---\n\n\ndef create_session(camp_id, session_id, starts_at, duration_minutes, agenda):\n    \"\"\"Create a scheduled session for a campaign.\n\n    Returns the saved session on success, None if the campaign is missing,\n    or False if the session id already exists in the campaign.\n    \"\"\"\n    import json\n\n    with _get_db() as conn:\n        if conn.execute(\"SELECT 1 FROM campaigns WHERE id = ?\", (camp_id,)).fetchone() is None:\n            return None\n        if conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT 1 FROM sessions WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?\",\n            (camp_id, session_id),\n        ).fetchone() is None:\n            return None\n\n        all_char_ids = set(present) | set(absent)\n        if all_char_ids:\n            placeholders = \",\".join(\"?\" * len(all_char_ids))\n            rows = conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT id FROM campaign_characters WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id IN ({})\".format(placeholders),\n                (camp_id,) + tuple(all_char_ids),\n            ).fetchall()\n            valid_ids = {r[\"id\"] for r in rows}\n            if valid_ids != all_char_ids:\n                return False\n\n        conn.execute(\n            \"DELETE FROM session_attendance WHERE campaign_id = ? AND session_id = ?\",\n            (camp_id, session_id),\n        )\n        for char_id in present:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO session_attendance (campaign_id, session_id, character_id, present) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                (camp_id, session_id, char_id, 1),\n            )\n        for char_id in absent:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO session_attendance (campaign_id, session_id, character_id, present) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                (camp_id, session_id, char_id, 0),\n            )\n        conn.commit()\n    return {\n        \"session_id\": session_id,\n        \"present_count\": len(present),\n        \"absent_count\": len(absent),\n    }\n\n\ndef get_session_count(camp_id):\n    \"\"\"Return the number of scheduled sessions in a campaign.\"\"\"\n    with _get_db() as conn:\n        row = conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM sessions WHERE campaign_id = ?\",\n            (camp_id,),\n        ).fetchone()\n        return row[\"cnt\"]\n\n\ndef get_play_campaign(camp_id):\n    \"\"\"Return a play campaign or None if missing.\"\"\"\n    with _get_db() as conn:\n        row = conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT id, name, owner, status, max_players, current_actor, turn_number \"\n            \"FROM play_campaigns WHERE id = ?\",\n            (camp_id,),\n        ).fetchone()\n        if row is None:\n            return None\n        return {\n            \"id\": row[\"id\"],\n            \"name\": row[\"name\"],\n            \"owner\": row[\"owner\"],\n            \"status\": row[\"status\"],\n            \"max_players\": row[\"max_players\"],\n            \"current_actor\": row[\"current_actor\"],\n            \"turn_number\": row[\"turn_number\"],\n        }\n\n\ndef create_play_campaign(camp_id, name, owner, max_players):\n    \"\"\"Create a play campaign; Validates input, delegates to domain/services/storage, and shapes JSON responses. |\n| `domain.py`       | Pure, side-effect-free D&D 5e math and static tables (XP, modifiers, dice, rests, etc.). |\n| `services.py`     | Higher-level workflows that combine domain logic with storage (e.g., encounter builder). |\n| `storage.py`      | SQLite persistence layer. All SQL lives here; routes never touch the database directly. |\n| `run.sh`          | Bootstrap and server start script.                                        |\n| `requirements.txt`| Flask dependency pin.                                                     |\n| `game.db`         | SQLite database file created automatically next to `app.py`.             |\n\n`app.py` is deliberately thin: it only wires the app together and initializes\nthe schema on startup.\n\n## State, persistence, and routing\n\n### Persistence\n\n- Storage is provided by SQLite in `game.db`.\n- The schema version is `1` and is hard-coded in `storage.py`.\n- `storage.init_db()` creates tables on startup; `storage.reset_db()` drops and\n  recreates them (used by `POST /v1/storage/reset`).\n- All tables use string primary keys for domain entities (campaigns, combat\n  sessions, users, compendium entries). Junction tables enforce composite keys.\n- Foreign keys are declared in the DDL but are not enabled at runtime; the\n  application enforces referential integrity through the storage layer.\n\n### Request routing\n\nRoutes are grouped in a Flask Blueprint (`api`) and registered in `app.py`.\nThe route layer does three things:\n\n1. Parse and validate the JSON body.\n2. Call the appropriate domain function, service, or storage function.\n3. Return the same JSON body and status code as the previous checkpoint.\n\nRoutes do not contain SQL or business math beyond input validation.\n\n### Determinism\n\n- No randomness is used in responses.\n- Initiative order, combat turn order, and condition decay are deterministic.\n- Passwords are hashed with PBKDF2; the token returned on login is deterministic\n  (`session-{username}`).\n\n## Main API groups\n\n### Core utilities\n\n- `GET /health` — liveness check.\n- `POST /v1/dice/stats` — statistics for expressions like `2d6+3`.\n- `POST /v1/checks/ability` — d20 ability check result.\n- `POST /v1/encounters/adjusted-xp` — encounter difficulty for level-3 parties.\n- `POST /v1/initiative/order` — deterministic initiative ordering.\n\n### Combat\n\n- `POST /v1/combat/sessions` — create a session and store combatants.\n- `POST /v1/combat/sessions/<id>/conditions` — attach a condition to a combatant.\n- `POST /v1/combat/sessions/<id>/advance` — advance the turn, decay conditions.\n\n### Characters\n\n- `POST /v1/characters/ability-modifier`\n- `POST /v1/characters/proficiency`\n- `POST /v1/characters/derived-stats`\n\n### Auth\n\n- `POST /v1/auth/register` — create a user with role `dm` or `player`.\n- `POST /v1/auth/login` — validate credentials and return a deterministic token.\n\n### Compendium\n\n- `POST /v1/compendium/monsters` and `GET /v1/compendium/monsters/<slug>`\n- `POST /v1/compendium/items` and `GET /v1/compendium/items/<slug>`\n\n### Campaigns\n\n- `POST /v1/campaigns`\n- `POST /v1/campaigns/<id>/characters`\n- `POST /v1/campaigns/<id>/events`\n- `GET /v1/campaigns/<id>/state`\n\n### Player's Handbook helpers\n\n- `POST /v1/phb/spell-slots`\n- `POST /v1/phb/rests/long`\n- `POST /v1/phb/equipment-load`\n\n### DM tools\n\n- `POST /v1/dm/encounter-builder` — builds an encounter from stored monsters.\n- `POST /v1/dm/loot-parcel` — fixed tier-1 loot parcel.\n- `POST /v1/dm/session-recap` — fixed recap for an existing campaign.\n\n## Conventions for extending and testing\n\n### Adding a new endpoint\n\n1. Put the route in `routes.py` inside the `api` Blueprint.\n2. Keep validation in the route; keep math in `domain.py` and persistence in\n   `storage.py`.\n3. If the operation needs both storage and domain logic, consider adding a\n   function to `services.py`.\n4. Return JSON error objects with an `error` key and the same HTTP status codes\n   as the existing routes (usually `400`, `401`, `404`, or `409`).\n\n### Adding persistence\n\n1. Add DDL to `storage.py` inside `_CREATE_TABLES`.\n2. Add a public storage function that returns a plain dict, `True`, `None`, or\n   `False` — never a raw `sqlite3.Row` or connection.\n3. Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` only when the schema changes in a way that requires\n   migration logic.\n\n### Testing\n\n- Use the Flask test client to avoid starting a real server:\n\n```python\nfrom app import app\nclient = app.test_client()\nclient.post(\"/v1/dice/stats\", json={\"expression\": \"2d6+3\"})\n```\n\n- For tests that mutate data, temporarily point `storage.DB_PATH` to a temp file\n  before importing `app` to avoid corrupting the production `game.db`.\n- Avoid calling `storage.reset_db()` against the real `game.db` from tests.\n- You can also smoke-test with `curl` against a running `./run.sh` process.\n\n### Things to preserve\n\nThis is a cumulative checkpoint.
